notes: §1985:VI.6.7.4 GR2: "A GO TO statement in a section whose segment-number is greater than or equal to 50 must not be referred to by an ALTER statement in a section with a different segment-number", and "All other uses of the ALTER statement are valid and are performed even if procedure-name-1 is in an overlayable fixed segment" (restated at §1985:XVI.3.3.1). Since kb/Work PB5084 BindAlter asks Segmentation.CheckAlter of each procedure-name-1, which compares the segment-numbers (Segmentation.ValueOf) and refuses an ALTER from another segment of a GO TO in segment 50-99 with COBOL6877, the first sentence the prior PARTIAL found missing; every other ALTER binds and EmitAlter stores the target. Probed at --std 85 (classes b, c): ALTER in segment 0 and in segment 61 of a GO TO in SECTION 60 are refused (6877); ALTER and GO TO both in SECTION 60, ALTER in segment 10 of a GO TO in fixed overlayable SECTION 40, ALTER in segment 0 of SECTION 49, and ALTER in SECTION 50 of a GO TO in SECTION 10 compile and display ALTERED; at --std 2002 ALTER is COBOL0810. The witness: ALTER and its GO TO both in SECTION 50, displaying ALTERED. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB5084 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5084 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-07.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-07-refute.json).
